sentences.text: Social worker Tom Ashby identified himself as being from the adult team at Coldmere and stated they had spoken on the phone prior to the meeting.
Lisa Keegan, identified as the person's daughter, stated she had taken the morning off.
Ronald Keegan agreed to Lisa Keegan staying while the conversation took place.
Ronald Keegan confirmed Pat was his wife and stated they had been married for forty-six years.
Ronald Keegan stated his wife died last March.
Ronald Keegan stated he was not managing well since coming home from Coldmere General, describing himself as 'bit stiff' and having a sore hip when going up stairs.
Ronald Keegan admitted to going up the stairs on his backside some nights.
Ronald Keegan noted there is only one rail on the stairs.
Ronald Keegan stated he cannot get into the bath since the fall.
Ronald Keegan stated he has a strip wash.
Ronald Keegan stated he microwaves dinners.
Ronald Keegan stated his wife Pat cooked all the meals.
Ronald Keegan stated it is quiet without his wife.
Ronald Keegan stated he used to go to the British Legion on a Friday but has not bothered lately.
Ronald Keegan stated he wants to stay in his house and does not want a home.
Ronald Keegan admitted he likes a drink and will not lie, stating he has a couple of cans of lager an evening and a couple of cans with his tea.
Lisa Keegan stated she clears the recycling and sees eight cans a day of the big strong lager, and that there is vodka.
Lisa Keegan stated she sees the empties in the bin every Sunday and has counted the cans at eight a day.
Ronald Keegan disputed Lisa Keegan's account of the drinking, stating it is only a couple of cans and that he is not hurting anybody.
Lisa Keegan stated Ronald Keegan had been drinking since dinner time when she found him in the morning.
Lisa Keegan stated Ronald Keegan fell in the kitchen after he had had a drink and was on the floor all night and could not get up.
Lisa Keegan stated this was not the first time, noting he fell in the hall in the summer after he had had a drink.
Ronald Keegan stated the previous fall was on the step.
Lisa Keegan reported that Mrs Okafor next door told her she saw Ronald Keegan driving to the Co-op after he had had a drink.
Lisa Keegan stated she had not seen Ronald Keegan driving herself as she was at work.
Ronald Keegan disputed Mrs Okafor's report, stating he only drives on Sundays to the cemetery and that Mrs Okafor wants to mind her own business.
The social worker noted that Mrs Okafor said to Lisa Keegan that she saw Ronald Keegan driving to the Co-op after he had had a drink, and that Ronald Keegan disputed this.
Ronald Keegan stated he has the state pension and the works pension from the foundry.
Ronald Keegan stated he receives about fourteen hundred a month.
Ronald Keegan stated he has never heard of Attendance Allowance.
Ronald Keegan stated he is not going to some meeting.
Ronald Keegan agreed to see the Coldmere alcohol service for just one chat.
Lisa Keegan stated she has been on at Ronald Keegan about a pendant alarm.
Ronald Keegan agreed to the pendant alarm.
The social worker agreed to refer Ronald Keegan to the occupational therapist for a stair rail and bathing assessment by the second of December.
Ronald Keegan agreed to the referral to Dr Haines at Bridge Street surgery regarding the falls and alcohol.
The social worker agreed to write to Dr Haines at Bridge Street surgery about the falls and the alcohol with Ronald Keegan's consent.
The social worker agreed to make the referral to the alcohol service this week.
The social worker agreed to arrange the pendant alarm through Careline.
Lisa Keegan agreed to do the Attendance Allowance form with the social worker on Sunday.
The social worker suggested Ronald Keegan think about attending the British Legion again on Fridays to help with the quiet.
Ronald Keegan stated Bill keeps asking him about the Legion.
The social worker agreed to ring Ronald Keegan on the ninth of December to see how things are.
